newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan overnight rate 0.53 pct, highest since April.
newsitem.headline: Japan overnight rate 0.53 pct, highest since April.

text.p: The weighted average of Japan's key overnight call rate rose to 0.53 percent on Thursday, the highest rate since April 3, 1996, traders said.
Traders said some banks in a hurry to raise funds at the short-end of the market were to blame for the rise in the key overnight rate.

Given a widespread view that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) will try to keep the key overnight call below 0.50 percent in the near future, banks prefered raising funds at the short-end of the market, although traders said demand was rising ahead of the fiscal year-end.

The BOJ continued to supply sufficient funds to offset a market shortage in the morning, but set repurchase agreements of the offered bills and T-bills within this fiscal year. Traders said players who were not expecting the action pushed the key overnight rate briefly as high as 0.55 percent.
